# CodeWiki parity baseline

This fixture pins the deterministic output of the legacy `gcode codewiki`
engine before ownership moves to `gwiki code`. The indexed input is exactly
`project/README.md`, `project/Cargo.toml`, and `project/src/lib.rs`; comparison
runs copy those files to a temporary project and never write inside the
committed project directory.

Pinned fixture input digest: `183aff969abb9300d8936911615245d3c9b6fe79e7ad5cbbe5ffbf017292f5a0`

## Frozen baseline and comparison

The `gcode codewiki` engine was removed after the ownership move, so
`baseline.sha256` is **frozen**: it cannot be regenerated, and the capture
block below is the permanent record of how it was produced. The script rejects
`--engine gcode` with a retirement error.

Compare `gwiki code` output through the shared normalization and manifest
implementation:

```sh
scripts/codewiki_parity_baseline.sh --engine gwiki
```

The comparison runs generation twice, requires the two sorted manifests to
match (same-engine determinism), and then requires them to match the frozen
baseline. The enumerated mode and parser branch can be checked without
execution:

```sh
CODEWIKI_PARITY_PARSE_ONLY=1 scripts/codewiki_parity_baseline.sh --engine gwiki
```

The run builds with `cargo build --locked`, runs the built target path
directly, indexes the copied fixture under the dedicated temporary identity
`019fe500-0000-7000-8000-000000019814`, generates into a fresh temporary
vault, and removes that identity from the index on exit. The copied project
gets a deterministic local Git commit so the engine emits its commit stamps;
the non-hashed capture record separately pins the actual workspace revision.
Set `CODEWIKI_PARITY_PRODUCTION_VAULT` when the production vault is not the
repository's `wiki/` directory; the harness refuses to put any run beneath the
configured path. The Rust harness in `crates/gwiki/tests/code_parity.rs` runs
the script only when `CODEWIKI_PARITY_HARNESS=1` is exported (it needs
PostgreSQL, git, and a nested cargo build).

## Normalization rules

The shared manifest path normalizes only the approved parity exceptions:

- `generated_by:` values and `gcode-codewiki` / `gwiki-code` marker strings;
- Markdown frontmatter `commit:`, `commit_dirty:`, and `generated:` values;
- JSON `commit`, `commit_dirty`, and `generated_at` values in
  `_meta/codewiki.json`, `_meta/truth_digest.json`, and nested records;
- the `invalidation_key` values for `code/_ownership.md` and
  `code/deprecations.md` in `_meta/codewiki.json`, which hash rendered
  frontmatter before provenance normalization and are pinned to their
  pre-move values (drift in those pages still surfaces through their page
  hashes); and
- `_meta/codewiki.lock`, which is synchronization state and is excluded.

Every other generated byte is hashed. The harness also requires a non-empty
page set and a `src/lib.rs` source hash in `_meta/codewiki.json`.
